notes.meaning: Instead of refreshing rain, God would send blinding dust and sandstorms upon the dry ground. Fierce winds would blow dust across the fields until the crops were ruined and the people faced famine. This shows that the land can only flourish when God provides water from above.

If Israel abandoned God, He would remove His protection in war, causing them to be defeated by their enemies. Instead of marching out as a united army, they would scatter in panic in seven directions and become an object of dread to the surrounding kingdoms. True safety in battle comes from the Lord alone.

The bodies of those killed in battle would be left lying in open fields, eaten by birds and wild animals. In the ancient world, being denied a burial was a terrible disgrace and showed that a person was cut off from God's favor.

Moses warns that God would strike the disobedient with terrible, painful skin diseases, similar to the boils that once plagued Egypt. These painful swellings, scabs, and severe itches would be incurable by human medicine because they came as divine judgment.

God would afflict the people with mental panic, confusion, and loss of understanding. Their minds would be so overwhelmed by distress and terror that they could no longer think clearly or plan wisely.

The people would grope around in confusion in broad daylight, like a blind person stumbling in the dark. Their plans would fail, and foreign oppressors would rob them continuously with no one to step in and save them.

A man would get engaged to a woman, only to have another man take her and violate her. An Israelite would build a house or plant a vineyard, but enemies would seize them before the builder or farmer could ever enjoy them.
Conquering enemies would slaughter a farmer's cattle and steal his donkeys and sheep right before his eyes. The owner would be completely powerless to stop the thieves or get his livestock back.

Parents would watch their sons and daughters be taken away into captivity by foreign invaders. Their eyes would wear out with weeping and longing for their children's return, but they would have neither the power nor the money to rescue them.

A strange, unknown nation would take over the land and devour all the crops the Israelites worked so hard to grow. The people would be left crushed, abused, and impoverished for the rest of their days.
The constant horrors of seeing family members taken, livestock stolen, and the land ruined would drive people completely mad. Helpless terror would rob them of their peace and sanity.

God would strike the people with painful, incurable boils covering their knees, thighs, and bodies from head to foot. These severe sores would make walking impossible and mark them as physically unclean under the law.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view this verse as a later addition or displacement because it returns to physical diseases after earlier verses had already moved on to military conquest.

notes.meaning: God would send both the people and their chosen king into exile in a distant, unfamiliar land. There, stripped of their freedom and true worship, they would be forced to serve worthless idols carved from wood and stone.
Among all the foreign nations where God scattered them, Israel would become a tragic spectacle and a target of mockery. Other people would laugh at their downfall and use their name as an insult.
Farmers would carry large amounts of seed out to their fields, but bring back very little food at harvest time. Swarms of locusts would arrive and eat up the sprouting grain before it could mature.
The people would work hard planting and caring for vineyards, but they would never drink the wine or gather the fruit. Destructive caterpillars and worms would devour the vines and ruin the harvest.
Olive trees would grow throughout their borders, but the olives would drop off the branches before ripening. As a result, the people would have no oil left for daily grooming, cooking, or anointing.
Parents would have sons and daughters, but would not get to keep or enjoy them at home. Enemy nations would carry the young people away as captives and slaves.
Relentless swarms of buzzing insects would sweep through the orchards and fields, eating every green leaf and piece of fruit. This total loss of produce would plunge the entire land into deep famine.

Foreigners living within Israel would prosper and rise higher and higher in wealth and power, while native Israelites would sink lower and lower into poverty. God's curse would turn their society upside down because of their rebellion.

The resident foreigner would become wealthy enough to lend money, while the impoverished Israelite would be forced to borrow. The foreigner would rule as the head, leaving Israel humbled at the bottom as the tail.

Moses concludes this warning by stating that these curses would chase down and overtake the people until they were completely ruined. These miseries were not random accidents, but the direct consequence of refusing to obey the Lord and follow His covenant commands.
